author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
I have observed this pattern.

When sr. engineers use AI, we try to shoehorn the AI into what we know that works from years of experience

When jr. engineers use AI, they end up reinventing the history of compute but with a twist of AI native.  They end up implementing a superior solution with the help of AI from the first principle because they don't have any baggage

author.name: Santosh Ahuja
author.headline: Engineering Executive | AI Infrastructure · GPU/Accelerator Systems · Distributed Systems · Silicon & Hardware-to-Cloud

comments.text: Fine, the junior's design is better. The question isn't who can fly with AI. It's who can read the instruments when the AI says we're on course and we're not. Experience is a liability when you're drawing the route and the only thing that saves you when the route is wrong.
